note: Adapted from Wilkinson's (1959) original description of the new species (in English), with complete prose descriptions and measurement tables for both the alate and the soldier (the table columns being Mean and Range). The author notes that the species is close to N. meruensis but distinguishable by the very large compound eyes and ocelli and by the short broad pronotum with a concave posterior margin; the soldier superficially resembles N. laticollis from the Seychelles. The phrase 'the remaining specimens' in the Chinese entry renders the original 'the rest'.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule pale brown and glossy; hairs sparse and minute, with one rather conspicuous hair behind each eye. Compound eyes black, large and strongly projecting. Ocelli white, oval and bulbous, very large, touching the compound eyes. Antennae pale yellowish brown, 18—21-segmented, mostly 20; segment 3 darker than the rest and slightly longer than segment 2. Labrum yellowish brown. Mandibles as figured. Pronotum in colour, surface and hairs as the head but with a few large bristles, usually 1 on the anterior margin, 4 on the lateral margins and 1 in the middle; broad and short, both anterior and posterior margins concave, the posterior and posterolateral angles usually distinct. Meso- and metathoracic scuta pale yellow. Wings transparent, the costa to the media brown; membrane slightly wrinkled; venation of the Neotermes type. Rest of the body pale white to yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi darker than the femora.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish brown, becoming red anteriorly; glossy, rather densely covered with minute bristles. Frons gently sloping with a V-shaped depression in the middle; head rather shallow, the sides converging anteriorly. Compound eyes black, the facets fine. Ocelli as small pale spots. Antennae yellowish brown at the base, paler towards the tip; 13—18-segmented, mostly 17; segment 3 club-shaped and very long, twice as long as segment 2; the other segments progressively elongate, the longest up to 3 times as long as wide. Labrum yellowish brown, evenly rounded at the tip. Postmentum concolorous with the head capsule, much broadened in front. Mandibles reddish brown at the base and black at the tip; hairy on the outer base; strongly upturned; tooth pattern irregular, as figured. Pronotum pale yellow; hairs as on the head; very broad, usually concave in the middle of the posterior margin. Rest of the body and legs pale yellow to pallid, claws and spurs reddish brown.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate measurements (20 specimens, mm; mean/range): head length to the anterior angle 1.53/1.39—1.75; head width at the compound eyes 1.79/1.68—1.94; ocellus length 0.24/0.20—0.27, width 0.18/0.16—0.20; greatest compound eye diameter 0.63/0.59—0.68; greatest pronotum length 1.03/0.91—1.17, greatest width 1.84/1.65—2.08; fore wing length 12.6/12.0—13.6, width 3.9/3.7—4.1; hind tibia length 1.59/1.46—1.75. Described from 62 specimens in 4 colonies (20 measured); the Marsabit population differs from the rest in the larger compound eyes and ocelli, the more numerous bristles and the strongly reddish brown tint of the back of the head. Soldier measurements (16 specimens, mm; mean/range): head length to the anterior angle 3.42/2.82—3.66; greatest head width 2.87/2.40—3.03; head width at the anterior angles 2.36/1.90—2.53; greatest head height 2.02/1.69—2.18; left mandible length 2.46/1.83—2.82; greatest pronotum length 1.62/1.12—1.83, greatest width 3.22/2.53—3.52; hind tibia length 1.85/1.19—2.04. Soldier described from 18 specimens in 6 colonies (16 measured).
